front: Demain, je parlerai au directeur.
back: Tomorrow I'll speak to the director.

front: Nous partirons tôt pour éviter les bouchons.
pronunciation: [noo par-tee-ROHN TOH poor ay-vee-tay lay boo-SHOHN]
back: We'll leave early to avoid the traffic.

front: Je prendrai le train de dix heures.
pronunciation: [zhuh prahn-DREH luh tran duh dee ZUHR]
back: I'll take the ten o'clock train.
context: -RE verbs drop the final e: prendre → prendr-.

front: Tu seras là à quelle heure ?
back: What time will you be there?
context: Irregular stems: être → ser-, avoir → aur-.

front: J'aurai trente ans en mai.
back: I'll be thirty in May.

front: Il fera beau tout le week-end.
back: It'll be nice all weekend.

front: Nous irons en Grèce l'été prochain.
back: We'll go to Greece next summer.

front: Je viendrai te chercher à la gare.
pronunciation: [zhuh vyan-DREH tuh shehr-shay ah lah GAR]
back: I'll come and pick you up at the station.

front: Vous pourrez visiter l'appartement samedi.
back: You'll be able to visit the apartment on Saturday.

front: Je verrai ce que je peux faire.
pronunciation: [zhuh veh-REH suh kuh zhuh puh FEHR]
back: I'll see what I can do.

front: Il faudra réserver à l'avance.
back: It will be necessary to book in advance.

front: Je saurai demain si j'ai le poste.
pronunciation: [zhuh soh-REH duh-MAN see zhay luh POST]
back: I'll know tomorrow if I got the job.

front: Tu devras travailler plus.
back: You'll have to work harder.

front: Ils voudront sûrement venir.
back: They'll surely want to come.

front: Quand tu auras fini, appelle-moi.
back: When you've finished, call me.
context: After 'quand' French uses the future (here futur antérieur), not the present as in English.

front: Quand je serai grand, je serai astronaute.
pronunciation: [kahn zhuh suh-reh GRAHN, zhuh suh-reh tas-troh-NOHT]
back: When I grow up, I'll be an astronaut.
context: 'Quand' + future in French ('when I will be big').

front: Dès que j'arriverai, je t'enverrai un message.
pronunciation: [deh kuh zhah-ree-vuh-REH, zhuh tahn-veh-reh tan meh-SAHZH]
back: As soon as I arrive, I'll send you a message.

front: S'il pleut, nous resterons à la maison.
pronunciation: [seel PLUH, noo res-tuh-ROHN ah lah meh-ZOHN]
back: If it rains, we'll stay home.
context: Si + present, then future. Never put the future after 'si' in this structure.

front: Je te promets que je ferai attention.
pronunciation: [zhuh tuh proh-MEH kuh zhuh fuh-reh ah-tahn-SYOHN]
back: I promise you I'll be careful.
context: Promises naturally take the futur simple.

front: Un jour, je vivrai au bord de la mer.
pronunciation: [an ZHOOR, zhuh vee-VREH oh bor duh lah MEHR]
back: One day, I'll live by the sea.

front: D'ici 2050, la population mondiale augmentera.
pronunciation: [dee-SEE duh meel san-KAHNT, lah poh-pü-lah-syohn mohn-DYAL ohg-mahn-tuh-RAH]
back: By 2050, the world population will increase.
context: 'D'ici' + date = by. Predictions in formal language use the futur simple.

front: Vous recevrez une réponse sous huit jours.
pronunciation: [voo ruh-suh-VRAY ün ray-POHNS soo wee ZHOOR]
back: You'll receive an answer within a week.
context: Recevoir → recevr-. 'Huit jours' = a week, 'sous' = within.

front: Je te le dirai quand je le saurai.
pronunciation: [zhuh tuh luh dee-REH kahn zhuh luh soh-REH]
back: I'll tell you when I know.
context: Future after 'quand' in both clauses: dirai, saurai. English uses the present ('when I know').

front: Ce sera tout pour aujourd'hui.
back: That'll be all for today.

front: Tu me manqueras.
back: I'll miss you.
context: Remember the reversed structure of manquer: 'tu me manqueras' = I will miss you.

front: Le magasin ouvrira ses portes en septembre.
pronunciation: [luh mah-gah-ZAN oo-vree-RAH say port ahn sep-TAHM-bruh]
back: The shop will open its doors in September.

front: Nous verrons ça plus tard.
back: We'll look at that later.
context: Postponing a topic in a meeting.

front: Je courrai le semi-marathon en avril.
back: I'll run the half marathon in April.
context: Courir → courr- (double r). Also mourir → mourr-.

front: Il y aura beaucoup de monde à la fête.
pronunciation: [eel yoh-RAH boh-koo duh MOHND ah lah FET]
back: There will be a lot of people at the party.

front: Je vais partir demain. / Je partirai demain.
pronunciation: [zhuh veh par-teer duh-MAN / zhuh par-tee-reh duh-MAN]
back: I'm going to leave tomorrow. / I'll leave tomorrow.
context: Futur proche (aller + inf.) is more spoken and immediate; the futur simple is more formal or more distant.

front: Le train partira à l'heure, sauf grève.
pronunciation: [luh tran par-tee-RAH ah LUHR, sohf GREV]
back: The train will leave on time, barring a strike.

front: Dans dix ans, tout aura changé.
back: In ten years, everything will have changed.
context: Futur antérieur: future of avoir/être + participle.

front: Rappelle-moi quand tu seras rentré.
back: Call me back when you get home.

front: Les résultats seront publiés lundi.
back: The results will be published on Monday.
context: Passive in the future: seront + participle.

front: Qui vivra verra.
back: Time will tell.
